question.value: What is the trigonometric parallax, distance and proper motion of the red transient V838 Mon from VLBA SiO maser astrometry, and what does ALMA show of its surroundings?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we report new VLBA observations of the 43 GHz SiO maser transitions toward V838 Mon. The phase-referencing technique was used to provide accurate astrometry.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00336.S.
V838 Mon was observed by ALMA in band 6 with four spectral ranges: 215.56–217.44, 219.06–220.94, 230.11–231.99, and 232.06–233.94 GHz (PI: T. Kamiński).
This corresponds to the SiO $v=0$, $J=5-4$ transition at 217 GHz
with the longest ALMA baselines of 15.3 km, which resulted in an angular resolution of 22 mas
resulted in an angular resolution of 22 mas (when imaged with Briggs weighting and with the robust parameter of 0.5)
The observations took place on 20 June 2019
(PI: T. Kamiński)
